analysis.evidence: The direct object אֶת כָּל אֵלֶּה refers to the animals Abram took. The next clause, וַיְבַתֵּר אֹתָם, describes him cutting them in two, with the birds excepted at the end of the verse.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ is prefixed to a Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular. The subject is Abram.
Hebrew direct-object particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: The phrase אֶת כָּל אֵלֶּה means “all of these.” אֵלֶּה points back to the animals just named, and כָּל includes the whole group in what Abram took.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the construct state before the plural demonstrative אֵלֶּה.
